nodes.name: Spontaneous Complex Formation
nodes.procedure: Polymer-salt complexes (PEG-Zn²⁺-aX⁻) (a = 1, 2, 3) formed spontaneously in aqueous electrolytes containing zinc (Zn²⁺) and halide (X⁻=Cl,Br,I) ions, specifically PEG300 readily forms complexes PEG300-Zn²⁺·aI⁻ (a = 1, 2, 3) with the unstable initial complexes [ZnI₃]⁻, [ZnI₂], and [ZnI]⁺ as confirmed by ¹H NMR showing strongest de-shielding effect in 5% PEG300 + 2 M ZnI₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals hexagonal platelet structures for Zn electrodeposits from ZnSO4 electrolytes and sphere-like structures from ZnX2 (X = Cl, Br, I) electrolytes, with large hexagonal platelets in ZnI2 + 5 wt% PEG300.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscope (SEM) images show that, hexagonal platelet electrodeposits form in ZnSO4 electrolytes (Figure 1C), whereas a thin scaffold consisting of inner unit sphere-like features form in aqueous ZnX2 (X = Cl, Br, I) electrolytes (Figure 1D–F).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows interfacial resistance of 158 Ω for ZnSO4, 161 Ω for ZnCl2, 1.1 Ω for ZnBr2, and 1.8 Ω for ZnI2 electrolytes on Zn plate surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Significantly, compared with the interfacial resistance of ZnSO4 and ZnCl2 electrolytes (158 and 161 Ω), ZnBr2 and ZnI2 exhibit remarkably small interfacial resistance, 1.1 and 1.8 Ω, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: 1H NMR confirms formation of stable PEG300-Zn2+-aI− (a=1,2,3) complexes in ZnI2 + PEG300 electrolytes through de-shielding effect causing right shift of PEG backbone 1H peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) was used to first understand the initial complexes formed in aqueous electrolytes containing Zn salts with PEG300. ... the 1H peak in the PEG backbone reflects the complexes stability of PEG300, Zn2+, and halide ions.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows larger and more stable I002:I101 peak ratio for Zn deposits in ZnI2 + 5 wt% PEG300 electrolyte than in ZnI2 alone, indicating highly (002) plane oriented deposition parallel to substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A) XRD analysis of Zn deposits after 24 min growth under galvanostatic conditions at a rate of 4 mA cm-2. B) The I002:I101 peak ratio deduced from XRD measurements for Zn deposit after 6, 12, and 24 min growth.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows uniform high density distribution of iodine and carbon (from PEG300) on Zn deposit surfaces parallel to substrate after washing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At different nucleation time points, the elements of iodine and carbon (carbon represents the PEG300) are observed to be uniformly distributed at high density on the exposed plane parallel to the substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows obvious Zn 2p and I 3d peaks on Zn foil cycled in ZnI2 electrolyte, but no peaks in ZnI2 + 5 wt% PEG300 electrolyte, indicating PEG300 coverage exceeds XPS sensitive thickness (10 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After cycling and washing with DI water, XPS analysis of the Zn foil shows obvious Zn 2p and I 3d peaks in the ZnI2 electrolyte (Figure S13A, Supporting Information), whereas there are no Zn 2p and I 3d peak in the ZnI2 + 5 wt% PEG300 electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: 2D grazing incident XRD profiles confirm crystal orientation differences for Zn deposits formed after 24 min growth in ZnI2 vs. ZnI2 + 5 wt% PEG300 electrolytes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: C,D) 2D grazing incident XRD profiles for Zn deposits formed after 24 min growth in 2 M ZnI2 and ZnI2+5 wt% PEG300 electrolyte, respectively, at 4 mA cm-2.
